passage: I am Dilnaz. For months I treated my evening run as the enemy of my marks, something to squeeze in if there was time. Then I started noticing things. Physics went best before dinner; after dinner my mind felt like wet cotton. And on days I ran first, even for fifteen minutes, my head felt clear. Lavanya, who runs with me, said, "So why is the run at nine?" I had no answer. I moved it to 5:15 and put the hardest study block right after. The run became the warm-up for thinking, not a rival. Some days I still skip it, but the days I do it are the ones when the hard chapters finally move.

How did Dilnaz think of the evening run before the change?
qa.a: As a rival to study time, which left Dilnaz torn and a little guilty about running. 🙂

qa.q: What could Dilnaz do on days when 5:15 is not possible?
qa.a: Take a short walk or stretch before studying, because the aim is a clear head before the hardest block.

qa.q: How might Lavanya see Dilnaz's old schedule?
qa.a: As odd, since Lavanya asked why the run was at nine.

grounding: Dilnaz notices hard subjects go best before dinner and a run clears the head, so a short run goes before the hardest study block.

Running club notes, Thursday — Kashish, Class 11
Last month Kashish told me she might drop running club because "boards are more important". Today she came with her own plan instead. She has noticed two things: her head works best for Maths between six and eight, before dinner, and after a run she feels "wiped clean, like a fresh page". So she has put a twenty-minute run at a quarter past five, a quick shower, and Maths at six. "The run isn't stealing from study," she said. "It's the warm-up." She showed me three days of notes: problems solved before and after the change. More after. I have moved her to the short-distance group so the run stays twenty minutes and doesn't tire her out.
— Omkar

qa.q: How does Kashish feel after a run, in her own words?
qa.a: She feels wiped clean, like a fresh page, which suggests she comes back calm and refreshed.

qa.q: What else could Kashish track to keep the plan working?
qa.a: Keep noting problems solved and adjust if a run ever leaves her too tired, so the schedule stays fitted to her energy.

qa.q: How does Omkar see Kashish's plan?
qa.a: Omkar supports it and adjusts the club to fit, moving Kashish to the short-distance group so the run helps rather than tires.

grounding: A coach's note shows a student placing a short run before her best Maths hours, treating exercise as a warm-up rather than a rival.

passage:
Wednesday
Tried the experiment again today. For two weeks I've noted when Physics actually goes in. Answer: 5:30 to 7:30. After dinner I'm useless, and straight after school I'm foggy. And on the days I went for a run first, the fog lifted faster. So today: home at 4:15, snack, then a fifteen-minute run round the colony park with Aditi trailing behind yelling, "Didi, slow down!" Shower, then Physics, the hardest chapter, from 5:30. Did eleven numericals and actually understood the last three. I used to think running was stealing study time. Now it's more like switching my brain on. English and easy reading after dinner, when I'm tired anyway.
Aadhya

qa.a: Eleven, and understood the last three.

qa.q: How did Aadhya feel about running before the experiment?
qa.a: Aadhya felt guilty about it, as if running were stealing study time.

qa.q: What might Aadhya try if rain stops the run?
qa.a: A short indoor activity like skipping or stretching before Physics, keeping the same brain-switching routine.

qa.q: What is the new routine like for Aditi?
qa.a: Aditi gets a daily run with her Didi, trailing behind and shouting, which she seems to enjoy even if she can't keep up.

grounding: A student's diary shows her noticing her best study hours and placing a short run before the hardest block.
